trust_decision.summary: stringprep decides the RFC 3454 B.2/B.3 case mapping for each code point (used by IDNA nameprep). Exceptions come from the b3_exceptions table; everything else falls back to str.lower(), which uses the interpreter's current Unicode case data, not Unicode 3.2.0. So code points that gained a lowercase mapping after 3.2 are mapped when the RFC says they should pass through unchanged.

landing_point.why: The advisory title names stringprep.map_table_b2(). An engineer would open that function first, then follow it into map_table_b3 and its str.lower() fallback at Lib/stringprep.py:192.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The only published site outside Lib/ is Tools/unicode/mkstringprep.py:176-180, a build-time generator that runtime tests cannot exercise. It does not fit any O2 kind as a runtime route.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the O8 route: unicodedata.ucd_3_2_0.normalize() is a C-level unicodedata feature, not stringprep, and the case-mapping report never mentions canonical ordering. Combining classes are also stable under Unicode policy, so the solver can argue that only newly assigned code points differ and that is a normalization concern outside the case-mapping advisory.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: nameprep runs with AllowUnassigned=true, so code points unassigned in 3.2 must keep passing through and not be rejected. Real B.2/B.3 mappings must keep working: ASCII and Latin lowercasing, and the special foldings such as U+00DF to 'ss' and U+0130 to 'i\u0307'. A fix that rejects every post-3.2 code point, or drops the str.lower() fallback, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: code points unassigned in Unicode 3.2 that case-fold today (e.g. Adlam U+1E900-U+1E921, fix.diff:18531-18539)
code points assigned in 3.2 that gained a lowercase mapping later (Cherokee, Georgian capital, Cyrillic Palochka, U+2183; test cases at fix.diff:18620-18625)
single code point via map_table_b3 vs whole label via map_table_b2 / idna nameprep (multi-label domain, trailing dot)

O7_producer.where: Tools/unicode/mkstringprep.py:176-180 builds b3_exceptions from the RFC 3454 tables. It needs rfc3454.txt (Tools/unicode/mkstringprep.py:50), which is not in the pinned tree. The runtime case data behind str.lower() comes from Objects/unicodectype.c:201.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ucd_3_2_0.normalize (used by nameprep NFKC and map_table_b2) reorders and blocks combining marks with the current combining class, while ucd_3_2_0.combining() treats code points unassigned in 3.2 as class 0. The two disagree on 3.2 behaviour for newly assigned marks.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is in the C unicodedata module, not stringprep. It concerns normalization, not case mapping. Combining classes are Unicode-stable for assigned characters.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Lib/stringprep.py -> Modules/unicodedata.c (Python lib -> C extension); same mismatch at Modules/unicodedata.c:697 and Modules/unicodedata.c:839, compared with Modules/unicodedata.c:325-330

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the ACE-prefix check runs label.lower() with current Unicode on the nameprep output. A sibling could lowercase the label with str.lower() before nameprep instead of via stringprep.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer could write a 'normalise case first' shortcut with str.lower(), not knowing it uses the current Unicode version.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a table predicate that calls the top-level unicodedata module (current version) instead of ucd_3_2_0, e.g. in a newly added helper
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix itself brings in the top-level 'import unicodedata' next to ucd_3_2_0 (fix.diff:18233-18238), so mixing up the two aliases is an easy mistake.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Hand-add identity entries to b3_exceptions for the few code points in the report (Cherokee, Georgian), or skip mapping for code points unassigned in 3.2, missing the assigned-in-3.2 code points that gained lowercase later.

out_of_scope_notes: Modules/unicodedata.c:183-200: ucd_3_2_0.digit() never consults the 3.2.0 change record, unlike decimal() and numeric(). Not used by stringprep.
Lib/urllib/parse.py NFKC netloc check uses the current unicodedata version; separate protection, not pursued.
unverified: Of the 14 fix commits, 6 are release roll-ups (3.10.22 to 3.15.0rc2) bundling unrelated security fixes, and c42790b only adjusts the generator. The behavioural backport for this pin is 1e54caa (fix.diff:18218-18919).

Fairness: a complete fix needs the RFC 3454 B.2/B.3 data or Unicode 3.2 case mappings. rfc3454.txt is not in the pinned tree, and ucd_3_2_0 exposes no case data, so an offline solver may not be able to rebuild the full exception list in 45 minutes.
O8 route: no specific code point was checked that is unassigned in 3.2, has a nonzero combining class today and changes nameprep output; the mismatch is shown from code only.
